Subject: Advance credit & ramp structure — Starlit AI (startup)

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — the latency numbers look promising and the team is excited to move from PoC to production. We’re an early-stage ML startup (Series A, ~30 engineers) and are looking at a 12–24 month advance commitment to get predictable unit economics while we scale. A few specifics from our side: 

- Target first-year committed spend: $120,000 prepaid (we can split across 12 months or do an upfront payment).
- We expect an adoption ramp: month 1–3 light, months 4–9 growing, months 10+ steady; attached is a brief forecast.
- As a startup, we need: an intro discount for the upfront term, a credits buffer (to protect spikes) that rolls forward for 3 months, and clarity on how overages are billed.

Questions:
1) For a 12‑month vs 24‑month prepaid commitment, what tiered discount do you offer?
2) Can credits be structured as a refundable buffer or at least transferable between projects within our org?
3) Do you offer ramped minimums (e.g., lower initial monthly draw that steps up) and how do they affect the effective discount?

We’re trying to balance cash & runway with the need to lock in predictable pricing. Happy to hop on a short call — I can loop in our Head of Ops if needed.

Best,
Sara Ghosh
Head of ML — Starlit AI
[sara@starlitai.com]
[Attachment: starlit-usage-forecast.xlsx (XLSX, 28 KB)]

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the forecast.

Quick summary up front: yes, we can structure both 12 and 24 month advance commitments with tiered discounts and a rolling credit buffer. There are a few knobs to tune (effective discount, credit expiry, ramp schedule) that materially change unit economics, so I’ve looped in Monica (revops) and Vivek (startup sales lead) to propose a concrete option.

Proposed next steps:
- Monica: can you draft a 12m and 24m term sheet with (a) straight prepay split vs. fully upfront, (b) a 3‑month rolling credits buffer, and (c) a ramped minimum schedule (months 1–3: 25% of monthly target; months 4–9: 75%; months 10+: 100%).
- Vivek: I’ll let you add the commercial carve-outs for startup credits.
- Sara: if you’re comfortable, we’ll share a term sheet and a DocuSign link for a preliminary agreement — no legal redlines at that stage, just the commercial framework.

I’ve pulled a quick estimate offline — for $120k prepaid on a 12m term we can do a 15% effective discount off list for hosted API plus a $5k rolling credit (3 months expiry). For 24m we can push to 22% if they commit to the higher monthly run rate and agree to a 6‑month lock. I’ll let Monica add the math and attach the draft terms.

Cheers,
Alex Martinez

Subject: RDW commercial proposal: Starlit AI — 12m & 24m options

Hi Sara — following Alex’s note I prepared two compact options (summary here; full terms attached):

Option A — 12 months (recommended for runway preservation)
- Total prepay: $120,000 (can be paid upfront or in equal monthly installments).
- Effective discount: 15% off list rate across hosted-token pricing.
- Rolling buffer credits: $5,000 that roll forward for up to 3 months. Credits apply first to consumption and then overages billed monthly.
- Ramped minima: months 1–3: 25% of monthly baseline; months 4–9: 75%; months 10–12: 100%. If actual draw < ramped minima, unused prepay remains as account credit; no chargebacks.
- Overages: billed at post-discount list rate, with one free month to allow initial smoothing.

Option B — 24 months (for predictable unit economics)
- Total annualized commitment: $115,000/year equivalent (effective 22% discount vs list when annualized and committed for 24 months).
- $8,000 rolling buffer credits, roll-forward up to 6 months.
- Ramped minima can be shallower: months 1–3: 40%; months 4–6: 70%; months 7+: 100%.
- Early termination: pro-rated refund of unused credits after 90 days, less an administrative fee.

Notes and caveats:
- Credits are account-scoped (transferable between projects within the same org) but not refundable to cash except under the narrow termination clause above.
- We recommend the 12m option with monthly installments if you want to preserve runway and keep flexibility; if you need lower unit cost and predictable spend over two years, option B is better.

Attached: RDW-Termsheet-StarlitAI-v1.pdf (commercial summary + example pricing schedule).

If this looks good, we’ll send a DocuSign with the commercial term sheet and include an appendix for the ramp schedule and reporting cadence.

Thanks — Monica Patel
Revenue Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Monica and Alex — this is very close to our needs. A few clarifications and a small counter-proposal: 

1) For the 12m option, can the $5k rolling credits be split such that $3k is immediately usable and $2k is reserved for unexpected spikes (still roll-forward for 3 months)? That helps our cash planning.
2) Can we get a 2‑month trial where overages in months 1–2 are billed at the discounted rate (i.e., treated as part of the prepaid discount) to reduce risk?
3) On transferability: we will have multiple GCP projects under one billing entity. Can credits be applied across projects if we provide the billing account ID?

If you can confirm those three items, we’ll sign a preliminary commercial term sheet and loop in legal for final redlines. We will also start an internal approval to move the prepay to our finance team.

On timing — we’re aiming to close by 9/3 to hit our engineering sprint timelines.

Thanks,
Sara
